seo_description: Henderson caps how many inoperable vehicles a property may keep, and the number depends on your zoning designation. What the rule says, and what to do next.
hero_heading: How Many Inoperable Vehicles You Can Keep in Henderson
hero_description: Henderson does not leave this to interpretation. The city's property maintenance code puts a number on it, and the number depends on how your property is zoned.

sections.heading: Henderson Puts a Number On It
paragraphs: Most people worrying about a dead car in the driveway are working from a vague sense that someone might complain. In Henderson there is something more specific to work from. The city's property maintenance code limits how many inoperable or unregistered vehicles a single property may keep, and that limit is tied to the property's zoning designation rather than applied as one flat figure across the city.

Properties in an RNP-1 designated area are allowed up to six. RNP-2 areas are allowed up to four. Every other property is limited to two. So the first useful question is not whether anyone has noticed the vehicle, but which of those three categories your address falls into — because that single fact decides whether you are comfortably inside the limit or already over it.

There is a second condition attached. Where the code permits vehicles to be kept, they have to be screened by a substantially opaque fence at least six feet high. Screening is a requirement placed on vehicles that are already within the permitted number, not a way of putting an extra one out of sight.

sections.heading: The 72-Hour Allowance, and What It Does Not Cover
paragraphs: The code makes one narrow allowance for a vehicle that is actually being worked on. A single inoperable vehicle that is registered to a resident of the property and undergoing minor repair work may sit there for a period not exceeding 72 hours.

Three things in that sentence do the work. It covers one vehicle, not several. The vehicle has to be registered to somebody who lives at the property, which rules out a car parked there as a favour to a relative or a friend. And 72 hours is three days — short enough that a project waiting on a part, a payday or a free weekend will run past it without anyone intending to break a rule.

The code defines what counts as minor repair work elsewhere in its own text, and that definition is worth reading before relying on this allowance, because it is the part that decides whether the exception applies to your situation at all.

sections.heading: Three Things Worth Checking Before You Decide Anything

blocks.heading: Which designation your property carries
paragraphs: Six, four or two is a wide spread, and the difference between them is not something you can judge by looking at the street. It is worth confirming rather than assuming, since it sets the number everything else is measured against.

blocks.heading: How many vehicles actually count
paragraphs: The limit covers vehicles that are inoperable or unregistered. A car that still carries current plates but has not started in a year is worth thinking about honestly, because the count is about the vehicle's condition and registration rather than about how long it has been there.

blocks.heading: Whether screening is genuinely in place
paragraphs: A substantially opaque fence at six feet is a specific standard. A gate that stands open, a carport, or a tarp is not the same thing, and the difference matters more than it looks like it should.

sections.footnote: Henderson is an incorporated city and enforces this through its own code enforcement office, so this is the city's rule rather than a county one.

sections.heading: Bring It Into Line, or Let It Go
paragraphs: Once the number is clear the choice usually resolves quickly. If you are inside the limit and the screening is genuinely there, keeping a project vehicle is a legitimate position and there is no reason to rush it.

If you are over the number, the options are narrower than they first appear. Building compliant screening is real money and real work. Registering or repairing a vehicle you were never realistically going to finish tends to postpone the problem rather than solve it. Selling the one you care least about is often the cheapest way to get back under the line, and it is the option people tend to reach last rather than first.
If that is where you land, call {phone} and describe what you have — the year, make, model and condition, and whether it runs. That is enough to tell you where you stand.

sections.heading: If Selling Is the Simpler Answer

items.note: The category most often at issue here — a vehicle that will not start is inoperable by any reading.
Collision or storm damage that was never repaired, whether or not it still carries plates.
Ordinary cars that stopped being driven and quietly became part of the count.

faq.question: How many inoperable vehicles can I keep on my property in Henderson?
faq.answer: It depends on your zoning designation. RNP-1 areas are allowed up to six, RNP-2 up to four, and every other property is limited to two inoperable or unregistered vehicles.

faq.question: Does it help that the car still has current plates?
faq.answer: The limit covers vehicles that are inoperable or unregistered, so a registered vehicle that cannot be driven is still the kind of vehicle the rule is written about. Current plates alone do not take it out of the count.

faq.question: I am part-way through fixing it. How long do I have?
faq.answer: The code allows a single inoperable vehicle registered to a resident of the property and undergoing minor repair work for a period not exceeding 72 hours. What qualifies as minor repair work is defined elsewhere in the code and is worth checking before you rely on it.

faq.question: Can I just put it behind a fence?
faq.answer: Screening is required for vehicles that are already within the permitted number — a substantially opaque fence at least six feet high. It is a condition attached to vehicles you are allowed to keep, not a way of adding one beyond the limit.

final_cta.heading: Get a Number Before You Decide
final_cta.intro: Knowing what the vehicle is actually worth makes the choice between keeping it and selling it a much shorter conversation.
